audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Missing stabilizer normalization in ordered signed cycles; Zero-dimensional family contradicts the main equivalence and simplicity criterion; Unnormalized arithmetic twists need not preserve the tensor unit
limitations: P1 — Missing stabilizer normalization in ordered signed cycles — Counterevidence: Definitions5.16/5.19 and ordinary wedge p1120 include the stabilizer divisor; p1140 explicitly supplies1/N(alpha). Strong evidence of intended normalization; no counterexample to repaired positive-dimensional main theorem is claimed.

P2 — Zero-dimensional family contradicts the main equivalence and simplicity criterion — Counterevidence: The point case is excluded by intended positive dimension in several later uses. No positive-dimensional counterexample is inferred.

P3 — Unnormalized arithmetic twists need not preserve the tensor unit — Counterevidence: Exact cited Lawrence–Sawin v4 Definition2.4 imposes trivial identity restriction. This protection is present in the actual main application.

P4 — Line-valued pairings and translating families require similitude/scalar qualifications — Counterevidence: A finite torsion multiplier vanishes after finite étale cover; every derived subgroup kills a scalar character. Big monodromy asks for a normal subgroup, compatible with similitudes.
P5 — Wedge reconstruction incorrectly permits r=1 — Counterevidence: Theorem7.3 already assumes1<r≤n/2; the proof uses the r≥2 symmetric-power smoothness criterion.
Limitations: Initial review only; scientific_decision pending, human_reviews empty. No independent acceptance or independently verified runtime/UI identity.
Limitations: The reviewed primary object is the exact author-hosted journal-typeset PDF; the arXiv v3 PDF/TeX are ancillary and not assumed identical to the journal or its production source.

Limitations: Collective reading covers the journal, but proof reconstruction and dependency validation are bounded by the explicit coverage records; no complete reproof of generic vanishing, BBD, microlocal Tannaka theory, SGA/Milne, Larsen alternatives, or full minuscule classification is claimed.

Limitations: Full-length type-D reducedness in Lemma5.22 remains unclosed: a quotient-lattice test defeats the formal collision/transitivity argument, but no actual perverse-sheaf or conormal realization is known from this check. It is not an established counterexample or numbered Problem.
Limitations: The factorial, parity identity and support-preserving repair are verified; they do not independently certify every remaining geometric step or author adoption.
Limitations: Source searches identified no specific correction at the inspected publication entry; they do not prove absence of an erratum or first discovery.
Limitations: No positive-dimensional counterexample to the intended main theorem after the identified corrections was established.

Limits: Finite enumeration confirms stated counts and sample identities. The all-n normalized parity identity additionally has a direct involution proof. No finite computation is advertised as all of the geometric classification.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

repair.content:
Quotient-normalize equal-coefficient ordered slots; divide byn! in all-ones spin case; align p1135 delta sign. State absolute-value/parity conventions for general signed type-D weights.

State d>0/nontriviality in the affected theorems, minuscule statement and numerical lemma, or handle the unit object separately.

Require e*Lχ trivial as Galois representation with normalized multiplicative structure, or restrict the lemma to an algebraically closed field.

Use the appropriate similitude group; qualify finiteness by torsion and distinguish full from derived monodromy.

Require r≥2 in Theorem7.6.
